# Aura3D (full agent guide)

> Aura3D: the TypeScript 3D engine that ships the whole stack — typed scenes, looks, typed GLB/glTF assets, camera rigs, gameFeel, and gameplay through `@aura3d/engine` plus the `@aura3d/cli` toolchain, for browser 3D apps and interactive websites. Start with https://aura3d.auraone.ai/llms.txt (fast path); this file is the long form.

Typed lighting looks, licensed and hashed GLB assets, a game kit and deploy checks in one TypeScript 3D engine for the browser. Built for AI coding agents.

## Facts

- Product: AI-native TypeScript 3D SDK for browser 3D apps, interactive websites, and prompt-to-code scene kits
- Website: https://aura3d.auraone.ai
- Current release: Aura3D 4.6.0 (per the repo manifest — the same source the build's version guard uses)
- Docs: https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/api.html
- Showcase game: https://aura3d.auraone.ai/showcase/aura-clash/
- Sitemap: https://aura3d.auraone.ai/sitemap.xml
- Crawl policy: https://aura3d.auraone.ai/robots.txt (public content allow-all; build internals and source maps disallowed)
- Last updated: 2026-10-29

## Notes

- Domain: https://aura3d.auraone.ai is a placeholder — swap AURA3D_SITE_URL (or the generator's ORIGIN) at deploy time; every URL in robots.txt, sitemap.xml, and these files follows.

<!-- agent-guide: everything below this marker is the long-form agent guide; gen-seo.mjs preserves it verbatim -->
Aura3D agent guide — a typed scene API for building real 3D apps: scenes, looks,
lighting, materials, typed assets, camera rigs, gameFeel, SDF text, decals, rigid bodies, and gameplay through
`@aura3d/engine` plus the `@aura3d/cli` toolchain. Current release: see Facts above. It includes the game kit, QA replay hooks, safety net, audio synth, model loader, GLSL chunks, scatter/merge helpers, racket-sports kits and CLI asset tools.

Hello world: every scene gets a look first.

```ts
import { createAuraApp, looks, model, scene } from "@aura3d/engine";
import { assets } from "./aura-assets";

createAuraApp("#app", {
  scene: scene().add(looks.preset("product-studio")).add(model(assets.robot)),
  ...looks.appOptions("product-studio")
});
```

The quality floor — what the defaults give you, and the never list:

- A `looks.preset` supplies environment light (IBL), a shadow-casting key, fog,
  background and a post grade as one unit — never hand-wire
  `lights.ambient()` as the only fill, it flattens shading and kills IBL.
- Never a solid void background: the look's sky, biome or studio backdrop owns it.
- Never `pixelRatio`/`qualityProfile`/`safe-basic`/FXAA overrides or
  `replaceTextures: true` — `looks.appOptions(id)` carries the renderer contract.
- Never a hero subject made of primitives; `model(assets.x)` with a typed
  catalog asset.
- Never emissive cards or sprites faking reflections, puddles, splashes or glows —
  use the look's `post` grade and `effects.*`.
- Never CSS/DOM particles, overlays or labels standing in for rendered output;
  HUD lives in the DOM, the scene does not.
- Keep the key shadow at full strength with contact darkening at the subject's
  feet; fog or atmosphere carries depth to the horizon.

three.js → Aura3D mapping (corrected):

| three.js | Aura3D |
| --- | --- |
| `new THREE.Scene()` | `scene()` |
| `new THREE.Mesh(...)` + `new GLTFLoader()` | `model(assets.x)` (typed asset) |
| `new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(...)` | `camera.perspective(...)`, `camera.rigs.*` |
| `AmbientLight` | `lights.hemisphere(...)` or the look's environment fill |
| `DirectionalLight` key/fill | the look's `key`/`rim` slots |
| `scene.environment` + PMREM | `environments.preset|hdri`, `world.biome` |
| `toneMapping`/exposure | `output.preset` and the look's post grade |
| `setPixelRatio` | `quality: "auto"` via `looks.appOptions` |
| `castShadow = true` | `shadow: true` on the light/node |
| `EffectComposer` passes | `output.preset` + `effects.*` |
| `AnimationMixer` | `AnimationController` |
| `new OrbitControls(...)` | `interactions.orbit(...)` |

Effects, post-processing, atmospherics & VFX (`effects.*` in `@aura3d/engine`):
- Post-processing: `effects.bloom`, `effects.neonBloom`, `effects.cinematicBloom`, `effects.ambientOcclusion`, `effects.contactOcclusion`, `effects.contactShadows`, `effects.screenSpaceReflections`, `effects.depthOfField`, `effects.motionBlur`, `effects.colorGrade`, `effects.vignette`, `effects.filmGrain`, `effects.chromaticAberration`, `effects.antiAlias`, `effects.outline`
- Atmospherics & volumetrics: `effects.fog`, `effects.depthFog`, `effects.volumetricFog`, `effects.fogVolume`, `effects.lightCone`, `effects.auroraRibbon`, `atmosphere.setSky`, `atmosphere.setWetness`
- Particles, weather & trails: `effects.particles`, `effects.meshParticles`, `effects.rain`, `effects.snow`, `effects.flipbook`, `effects.trail`, `effects.beam`, `ResidentGPUParticleRenderer` (WebGPU compute)
- Game feel & genre kits: `game.feel` / `app.feel` (`hitStop`, `slowMo`, `damageFlash`, `speedLines`, `landingDust`, camera trauma), `game.platformer`, `game.racing`, `game.arcadeKart`, `game.grandPrixRoad`, `game.carSoccer`, `game.carSoccerPitch`, `game.racketSports`, `game.fallingBlocks`, `game.fighting`

Genre recipes (see `aura3d-art-direction/references/look-recipes.md`):

| Genre | Look | Camera + fov | Palette/accent | Atmosphere |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| platformer | `outdoor-day` | follow2d fov 50 | greens/sky/wood + gold | fog 0.0025 |
| racing | `golden-hour` | chase fov 60 | asphalt/orange/charcoal + amber | fog 30–180 m |
| fighting | `arena-fight` | fighting fov 45 | arena dark/rope/crowd + rim | haze cone |
| arena shooter | `space` | topDown fov 55 | space blue/graphite/teal + magenta | none |
| sports/table | `interior-industrial` | topDown fov 40 | turf/white/dark + ball | indoor haze |
| product | `product-studio` | orbit fov 35 | grey/white/metal + brand | none |
| character | `character-showcase` | orbit fov 40 | costume neutrals + rim | room haze |
| outdoor env | `overcast` | wide fov 55 | green/slate/fog blue + wildflower | fog 0.004 |
| interior | `interior-warm` | orbit fov 45 | wood/cream/spines + plant | dust shafts |
| night city | `night-city` | tele fov 35 | sodium/neon/asphalt + cyan | fog 15–90 m |
| space | `space` | orbit fov 60 | void blue/limb/stars + aurora | none |
| underwater | `underwater` | follow fov 50 | deep blue/teal/kelp + coral | scatter 0.03 |
| cinematic | `polar-night` | dolly fov 35 | aurora/snow/night + lantern | snow mist 0.006 |

The look-dev loop:

1. Pick the genre recipe row and 1–3 reference frames; write a 3-line look brief.
2. Build with the look preset and typed assets; no renderer overrides.
3. Capture `aura3d look capture --route / --shots opening,mid,action`.
4. Judge each frame against the quality-bar rubric; read `aura3d look lint`.
5. Fix the single highest-leverage thing; one change per round; repeat until
   every category reads 7+ or the loop exits flat.

Assets — resolve real objects from the catalog first. Do not invent asset paths,
URLs or ids — every model comes from a generated `assets.<key>`:

- `npx @aura3d/cli@latest assets search "<object>"` (natural descriptive phrase;
  it searches licence-tagged open public sources and a starter pack (there is no Aura3D-run search service to rely on);
  results are candidates to check, not guaranteed matches).
- `assets resolve "<object>" --name <name>` pulls the top auto-pullable match
  and types it as `assets.<name>` → `model(assets.<name>)`.
- Add local files with `assets add ./assets/model.glb --name model`, then read
  the generated `src/aura-assets.ts`.
- Playable characters: `assets resolve "animated humanoid fighting character"
  --profile fighting-character` keeps provenance in `aura.assets.json`.

Scaffold:

```bash
npx create-aura3d@latest my-scene --template product-viewer
npx create-aura3d@latest my-fighter --template fighting-game
cd my-scene && npm run dev
```

Mandatory 3D game & scene anti-failure guardrails:

1. No primitive-box characters, vehicles, or hero props ("no stick-figure humans or box cars") & prop normalization (`targetMaxDimension` vs `targetHeight`):
   - Never assemble characters, athletes, enemies, vehicles, aircraft, trees, or architectural landmarks out of `primitives.box`, `primitives.sphere`, or `primitives.cylinder` — keep every silhouette, look, lighting, and shadow readable with real 3D geometry.
   - Every character, vehicle, creature, weapon, and landmark must mount a real 3D GLB via `model(assets.<name>, { targetMaxDimension, role })` from `src/aura-assets.ts` (use `targetHeight` only for upright humanoids and `targetMaxDimension` for horizontal vehicles, rackets, paddles, weapons, barriers, and wide props so aspect ratios and silhouettes never stretch vertically). If the catalog lacks a required 3D model, generate a bespoke PBR 3D model with Meshy (`meshy`) and admit it via `aura3d assets import-meshy`.
   - Drive rigged humanoid and creature GLBs (`skins > 0`) via `handle.setAnimation({ clip, loop: true, speed })` (or `AnimationController`) synchronized to locomotion (`idle`, `walk`, `run`, `attack`, `swing`) so limbs articulate under the key light and shadow instead of sliding rigid statues across the floor.
   - Primitives (`primitives.plane`, `primitives.box`, `primitives.cylinder`, `primitives.torus`) are reserved strictly for ground/court surfaces, field lines, UI rings/reticles, laser beams, and invisible physics colliders.
2. Boot sequence gate (`await app.ready()`) & default manual control (`autopilot = false` on Frame 1):
   - Gate Frame 1 on `await app.ready()` before fading out `#boot-gate` (`opacity: 0; pointer-events: none` then remove) and starting the gameplay simulation loop so lighting, shadow, and GLB silhouettes never pop in mid-frame.
   - Default `autopilot` / AI demo mode to `false` (immediate manual control on Frame 1 once `#boot-gate` clears); enable AI autopilot only when `?autoplay=1` or `?demo=1` is present in the URL or when the user clicks the HUD `Auto` toggle button, and yield back to manual control on keyboard (`keydown`), pointer, touch, or gamepad input.
   - Keep mode, stage, camera, `Auto`, and roster selectors in a compact, non-blocking top HUD bar that preserves camera framing, and always call `button.blur()` after button clicks so `Space` or `Enter` gameplay keys never re-trigger focused HUD buttons.
3. Always optimize Meshy 3D GLBs before admission (`aura3d assets optimize --file in.glb --out out.glb --role <role>`):
   - Raw Meshy exports often contain `200,000–1,750,000` vertices and `20–65 MB` of uncompressed 4K PNG textures, which stall main-thread glTF parsing and exhaust GPU memory when multiple models load in one scene.
   - Role budgets: prop 6,000, background 15,000, character 30,000, hero or vehicle 40,000 vertices; textures capped at 1024 to 2048 px; 16-bit indices; keep a game's assets near 25 MB. Admit in an isolated project (`assets import-meshy <dir> --into <assets-dir> --prefix <game> --name <role>`), never from the repo root while other work is open.
4. Always use canonical typed asset manifest refs (`hash` required):
   - The production glTF bridge requires `createAssetProvenance(node.asset).source === "typed-aura-assets-manifest"`, which requires a valid 64-character `sha256-...` `hash` and `public/aura-assets/...` provenance from `aura.assets.json` / `src/aura-assets.ts` so the rendered look and silhouette load cleanly.
   - Never omit `hash` in custom `defineAssets(...)` declarations and never place unhashed duplicate GLBs in route-local `apps/<route>/public/aura-assets/` that collide with root `public/aura-assets/`.
5. Mutate node handles instead of calling `app.setScene()` on every restart:
   - Do not call `app.setScene()` when restarting a round, hole, or bout on the same stage/world; tearing down and remounting the scene disposes live GPU resources, breaks lighting and postprocess continuity, and aborts in-flight GLB loads. Track a scene signature (`stageId` / `worldId`) and reset positions, visibility, and animations through runtime node handles (`app.nodes.require(...)`).
6. Prevent fog whitewash, overexposure, and instanced emissive blowout:
   - If a fast route whitewashes, pass `{ fogDensityScale: 0, exposureEv: -0.1 }` to `looks.preset(...)` for that route. Never pin post-processing, the compiler or fog off for every player with a `qualityRebuild.flags` list: it hides bugs and flattens the look. Install `installSafetyNet` from `@aura3d/debug` so a machine that renders black steps down one rung on its own and `?diag=1` shows the GPU, limits and shader failures.
   - Never set `emissive: "#ffffff"` with high `emissiveIntensity` on an instanced pool material (`instances.box` / `primitives.box({ instances })`): per-instance `instanceColors` multiply `u_baseColor`, not `u_emissiveColor`.
7. Ground `model()` feet on platform top surfaces (`y + sy / 2`) & wind custom meshes CCW:
   - `model(asset, { targetHeight })` normalizes the GLB with `minY = 0` (feet at `position[1]`), whereas `primitives.box` and `primitives.cylinder` (`instances.box` / `instances.cylinder`) are centered on `[-0.5..+0.5]` so a platform at `(y, sy)` has its top surface at `y + sy / 2`. Always place grounded characters and vehicles at `platform.y + platform.sy / 2` so they never sink into logs, pads, or road lanes. Wind custom `geometry.custom` triangles CCW when viewed from `+Y`.
8. Enforce full-viewport `100vw × 100vh` canvas, deep ground apron, and pushbox separation:
   - Size `html, body, #app, canvas` to `100vw × 100vh` (`position: fixed; inset: 0; overflow: hidden`) and extend the 3D ground/stage apron deep enough in `+Z`/`-Z` under the camera frustum so the bottom third of the viewport never shows a black clear-color void. Disable `collision: true` on `camera.rigs.shoulder` when the target character has attached child runtime nodes, and enforce `>= 1.4m` fighter pushbox separation (`|x| >= 1.8m` at spawn).


Kits (build the shell from these, do not hand-roll it):

- `@aura3d/engine/game`: `createGame` (lifecycle, pause, results, DOM HUD, touch, juice, game sound); the root `createGame` is a headless stub.
- `@aura3d/engine`: `createFixedStepLoop`, `installQaHooks` (`window.__AURA_<NAME>__`), `readQaParams`, `createCountedRng` for deterministic replay and automated checks; `defineModelAssets` for hashed same-origin models with a `?models=0` procedural fallback; `scatterAlongPath`, `scatterInArea`, `splitScatterByDistance`, `mergeStatic` for draw-call budgets; `game.racketSports()` with `ballFlight`, `scoring`, `athleteRig`.
- `@aura3d/engine/audio`: `createCueBank`, `createStepSequencer`, `createToneLoop`, `createSampleSlices` on the single `AudioContextManager` (never `new AudioContext(`).
- `@aura3d/debug`: `installSafetyNet` (`?diag=1`, quality switches `?post=0 ?shadow=0 ?env=0 ?sky=0 ?quality=low`, black-frame self-heal).
- `material.custom` shaders: `#include <a3d_math>`, `<a3d_noise>`, `<a3d_sky>`, `<a3d_fog>`, `<a3d_triplanar>`, `<a3d_toon>`, `<a3d_shadow>` (sun shadows: `receiveShadow: true` on the spec, then multiply the lit term by `a3dSunShadowAuto(worldPos, normal)`), `<colorspace_decode>`; custom shaders write linear light, so use `a3dSrgbToLinear` with `toneMapping: "none"` for authored colours, and keep `pow`, `normalize`, `sqrt` and divides NaN-safe (Apple GPUs return NaN where software renderers do not).
- Production checks that CI missed: the bridge refuses http(s) or unhashed model URLs and then draws nothing; instanced and batched meshes honour texture maps; empty instance arrays are no-ops; software-GL passes are not real-GPU proof. Docs: `docs/api/game-kit.md`, `qa-kit.md`, `safety-net.md`, `audio-synth.md`, `model-loader.md`, `glsl-chunks.md`, `scatter-merge.md`, `cli-asset-tools.md`; pitfalls: `aura3d-core/references/pitfalls.md`.

Claims: use every feature freely. Claim only what a judged capture shows.

- Label every capability as one of: `createAuraApp` root safe API,
  `production-runtime`, `rendering` internals, CLI asset pipeline, template-only
  scaffold, prototype, or roadmap.
- Public examples prove only what the safe API renders through `@aura3d/engine`.
- A compiling route is not proof: route health, typed provenance and a readable
  frame are required.

Release integrity rules:
- no raw string asset IDs, raw GLB/glTF URLs, `unsafeModelUrl(...)`, `three` imports, or `GLTFLoader` in public examples;
- no primary character, vehicle, product, weapon, creature, world, or hero environment made only from primitives unless the route is explicitly abstract visualization;
- no CSS/DOM particle implementation for examples claiming Aura3D particle rendering;
- no WebGPU, PBR, postprocess, skinned animation, morph, or game-runtime claim without matching browser evidence;
- no public showcase or README claim that exceeds detected capability, route-health evidence, or screenshots.

Benchmark mode: if `aura3d look capture` is available, run the look-dev loop;
otherwise run finite commands (`npm install && npm run build`) then stop and
label the result `prototype`.

| Scene Kit | API | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Material lab | `sceneKits.materialLab()` | root-proven (partial advanced coat extensions) |
